```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_pbpk"))$reference`
* Article: [PLoS One 2016;11(9):e0162428](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0162428)
  (open access, with the SBML and CompuCell3D model code as S2 File)

Sluka et al. built a three-scale model of acetaminophen (APAP) disposition:

1. a whole-body PBPK model (SBML, BioModels MODEL1509230010),
2. a two-dimensional agent-based model of blood flow and APAP exchange in a
   single hepatic sinusoid lined with 20 hepatocytes (Cellular Potts model in
   CompuCell3D), and
3. a subcellular reaction network for phase I and phase II metabolism run in
   each hepatocyte (SBML, BioModels MODEL1509230011).

The authors designed all three as standalone models that can be run on their
own (Results, "Standalone simulations") and showed standalone runs of each.
The two ODE modules are packaged here as separate models:

* `Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_pbpk`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_pbpk"))$description`
* `Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_hepatocyte_qsp`: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_hepatocyte_qsp"))$description`

The coupled multiscale model, which produces the paper's plasma APAP-glucuronide
and APAP-sulfate curves (Figs 7 to 12), the sensitivity analyses (Figs 13 to
16) and the population simulation (Fig 17), is not included: its liver is the
stochastic lattice model of point 2, which moves individual red blood cells and
serum portions along the sinusoid and exchanges drug between neighbouring
cells. That is not a system of ODEs and has no equivalent in rxode2.

# Population

No population model was fitted. The authors hand-tuned a parameter set named
REFSIM (Tables 2, 4 and 6; S1 File Table 10) so that the complete multiscale
model reproduced mean plasma concentrations of APAP and its glucuronide and
sulfate conjugates after a 20 mg/kg (1.4 g) oral dose of APAP syrup in nine
Caucasian volunteers (Critchley et al. 2005, paper reference 58): ages 23 to
44 years, body weight 55 to 97 kg, six men and three women (Results,
"Population Variability"). The digitised mean data are S1 File Table 15. Both
packaged models simulate one reference 70 kg man and carry no between-subject
variability and no residual error.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_pbpk")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The tables
below collect them.

## Whole-body PBPK module

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `bw` | 70 kg | Table 2 `pbpk_bw`; SBML `BW` |
| `qcc` | 15 L/h/kg^0.75 | S1 File Table 2 `QArt`; SBML `Cardiac_flow_ref` (363 L/h at 70 kg, Table 2 `pbpk_QCardiac` 363.01) |
| `fq_gut` | 0.205 | S1 File Table 2 `QGut` (74.4 L/h at 70 kg; Table 2 74.42) |
| `fq_liver` | 0.0535 | S1 File Table 2 `QLiver`, hepatic artery only (19.4 L/h; Table 2 19.42) |
| `fq_kidney` | 0.2214 | S1 File Table 2 `QKidney` (80.4 L/h; Table 2 80.37) |
| `q_other` | cardiac output minus gut, liver and kidney flows | S1 File Table 2 `QRest`; SBML assignment rule (188.8 L/h; Table 2 188.80) |
| `fvol_total` | 0.6 L/kg | SBML `VTotal_ref`; 42.0 L at 70 kg = S1 File Table 2 `VTotal` |
| `fvol_arterial`, `fvol_gut`, `fvol_kidney`, `fvol_liver`, `fvol_lung`, `fvol_venous` | 0.0357, 0.0263, 0.0070, 0.0408, 0.0121, 0.0812 | S1 File Table 2; volumes 1.50, 1.10, 0.294, 1.71, 0.508, 3.41 L match Table 2 |
| `v_other` | total minus the six named volumes | SBML initial assignment `VRest` (33.47 L; Table 2 33.47) |
| `lka` | log(1.5) | Table 2 `pbpk_kGutabs` 1.5 1/h |
| `fup` | 0.8 | Table 2 `pbpk_Fup` |
| `bp` | 1.09 | Table 2 `pbpk_Rb2p` |
| `lkp_liver`, `lkp_kidney`, `lkp_other` | log(1), log(1), log(1.6) | Table 2 `pbpk_Kl2p`, `pbpk_Kk2p`, `pbpk_Kr2p` |
| `qgfr` | 0.714 L/h | Table 2 `pbpk_Qgfr`; S1 File Table 10 REFSIM |
| `kmet` | 9.5 1/h | deposited SBML `CLmetabolism` (not printed in the paper tables) |
| ODEs | n/a | Table 1 rate equations; SBML reactions J1 to J13 |
| `Cvenous` | venous / v_venous | Fig 4 y-axis "Venous APAP" |
| `Cc` | Cvenous / bp | multiscale driver script `PBPK_SBML_MULTISteppables.py`: plasma = CVen / VVen / Rb2p |

# Whole-body PBPK module

## Simulation

The standalone run of Fig 4 is a single 1.4 g oral dose to a 70 kg man,
followed for 24 hours. Observation rows are placed on the venous-blood state,
so rxode2 returns both the blood (`Cvenous`) and plasma (`Cc`) concentrations.

```{r pbpk-sim}
mod_pbpk <- readModelDb("Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_pbpk")
dose_mg <- 1400

ev_pbpk <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_mg, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 24, by = 0.05), cmt = "venous")

sim_pbpk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pbpk, ev_pbpk, returnType = "data.frame")
```

## Replicates Figure 4

Fig 4 plots the venous whole-blood APAP concentration from the standalone
PBPK module against the plasma data of Critchley et al. The open symbols below
are those data as digitised by the authors (S1 File Table 15).

```{r pbpk-fig4}
critchley <- data.frame(
  time = c(0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 24),
  APAP = c(0, 8.94, 14.67, 16.77, 16.63, 14.89, 13.98, 10.85, 8.14, 6.12, 4.45, 3.13, 2.72, 1.20, 0.38),
  APAPS = c(0, 0.76, 1.97, 2.96, 3.41, 4.06, 4.24, 4.24, 3.71, 3.20, 2.68, 2.15, 1.66, 0.72, 0.12),
  APAPG = c(0, 0.33, 1.75, 3.65, 4.71, 7.74, 9.32, 10.78, 10.75, 9.48, 8.13, 6.78, 5.18, 2.05, 0.27)
)

sim_pbpk_long <- sim_pbpk |>
  dplyr::select(time, `Venous blood (Fig 4)` = Cvenous, `Venous plasma` = Cc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc")

ggplot(sim_pbpk_long, aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = matrix)) +
  geom_point(data = critchley, aes(time, APAP), shape = 0, size = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "APAP (ug/mL)", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Sluka 2016 (solid line). Squares: Critchley et al. plasma data (S1 File Table 15)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.75, 0.8))
```

Fig 4 peaks at about 17 ug/mL a little after 1 hour (read from the figure by
the maintainers). The packaged model gives:

```{r pbpk-fig4-check}
fig4 <- sim_pbpk |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax_blood = max(Cvenous),
    tmax_blood = time[which.max(Cvenous)],
    cmax_plasma = max(Cc)
  )
knitr::kable(fig4, digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value solve: no cohort, so a direct bound is safe.
  abs(fig4$cmax_blood - 17) / 17 < 0.05,
  fig4$tmax_blood > 0.9, fig4$tmax_blood < 1.5
)
```

## Mass balance and urinary recovery

The model is closed: drug leaves only into the kidney tubules (`a_urine`) or
by hepatic metabolism (`a_metabolized`), so the sum over all states equals the
dose at every time.

```{r pbpk-mass}
state_cols <- c("depot", "gut", "liver", "kidney", "other", "venous", "lung", "arterial", "a_urine", "a_metabolized")
mass <- sim_pbpk |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(state_cols))))
stopifnot(max(abs(mass$total - dose_mg)) / dose_mg < 1e-6)

recovery <- tail(sim_pbpk, 1) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    `Unchanged in urine (% of dose)` = 100 * a_urine / dose_mg,
    `Metabolized (% of dose)` = 100 * a_metabolized / dose_mg
  )
knitr::kable(recovery, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)
# Fig 17B (multiscale model): less than 10% of the dose is excreted as APAP.
stopifnot(recovery[[1]] < 10)
```

## PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA for the standalone PBPK module; S1 File Table 11
gives Cmax, Tmax and AUC for the complete multiscale model only. The
comparison below therefore uses the observed mean plasma profile of Critchley
et al. (S1 File Table 15) as the reference, analysed with the same PKNCA set
up as the simulated plasma profile.

```{r pbpk-nca}
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)

conc_sim <- sim_pbpk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = 1L, treatment = "1.4 g oral", time, Cc)
dose_sim <- data.frame(id = 1L, treatment = "1.4 g oral", time = 0, amt = dose_mg)

nca_sim <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_sim, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_sim, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals
))

conc_obs <- critchley |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = 1L, treatment = "1.4 g oral", time, Cc = APAP)
nca_obs <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_obs, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_sim, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals
))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_sim,
  reference = nca_obs,
  by = "treatment"
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Standalone PBPK plasma APAP (Simulated) against the Critchley et al. mean plasma data (Reference), both by PKNCA.")
```

Simulated plasma Cmax and AUC are within about 10% of the observed means. The
Tmax row is starred (more than 20% off): the simulated Tmax (about 1.2 h) is
later than the observed 0.75 h, as Fig 4 also shows. The authors later
re-examined absorption and concluded that APAP uptake from the gut lumen
behaves as a lag of about 9 minutes followed by zero-order (saturated
transporter) uptake, which fits early data better than the first-order
`pbpk_kGutabs` used in REFSIM (Results, "Advantages of Separate Models for the
Biological Scales"); they report no values for that variant, so it is not
packaged.
For context, the complete multiscale model with REFSIM gives a plasma APAP
Cmax of 16.01 ug/mL at 1.083 h and an AUC of 66.76 ug*h/mL over its 8 h run
(S1 File Table 11); those numbers come from a different liver model and are
not a target for the standalone module.

```{r pbpk-nca-check}
sim_res <- as.data.frame(nca_sim)
obs_res <- as.data.frame(nca_obs)
pct <- function(code) {
  s <- sim_res$PPORRES[sim_res$PPTESTCD == code]
  o <- obs_res$PPORRES[obs_res$PPTESTCD == code]
  100 * (s - o) / o
}
stopifnot(abs(pct("cmax")) < 15, abs(pct("auclast")) < 15)
```

# Hepatocyte subcellular module

## Replicates Figure 6

Fig 6 is the standalone run of the subcellular network from an initial
intracellular APAP concentration of 0.1 mmol/L (15 ug/mL), over 40 minutes.
Time in this model is in seconds.

```{r hep-sim}
mod_hep <- readModelDb("Sluka_2016_acetaminophen_hepatocyte_qsp")

ev_hep <- rxode2::et(amt = 0.1, cmt = "hep_apap") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 2400, by = 10), cmt = "hep_apap")
sim_hep <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hep, ev_hep, returnType = "data.frame")

sim_hep |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    minutes = time / 60, APAP = Cc, APAPG = Cc_apapg, APAPS = Cc_apaps
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-minutes, names_to = "species", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(minutes, conc, linetype = species)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (minute)", y = "Concentration (mmol/L)", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Sluka 2016."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Values read from Fig 6 by the maintainers: at 40 minutes APAP is nearly
exhausted, APAP-glucuronide has reached about 0.056 mmol/L and APAP-sulfate
about 0.042 mmol/L, and the falling APAP curve crosses the glucuronide curve
at about 10.5 minutes.

```{r hep-check}
end <- tail(sim_hep, 1)
cross_min <- with(sim_hep, time[which(Cc <= Cc_apapg)[1]] / 60)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("APAP at 40 min", "APAPG at 40 min", "APAPS at 40 min", "APAP = APAPG crossing (min)"),
  `Fig 6 (read)` = c("< 0.005", "0.056", "0.042", "10.5"),
  model = signif(c(end$Cc, end$Cc_apapg, end$Cc_apaps, cross_min), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
))

stopifnot(
  end$Cc < 0.005,
  abs(end$Cc_apapg - 0.056) / 0.056 < 0.05,
  abs(end$Cc_apaps - 0.042) / 0.042 < 0.05,
  abs(cross_min - 10.5) < 1.5
)
```

## Mass and glutathione balance

APAP is conserved across its four products, and glutathione is either free or
bound in the NAPQI conjugate, with resynthesis as the only source.

```{r hep-mass}
apap_total <- with(sim_hep, Cc + Cc_apapg + Cc_apaps + Cc_napqi + Cc_napqigsh)
stopifnot(max(abs(apap_total - 0.1)) < 1e-8)

knitr::kable(
  tail(sim_hep, 1) |>
    dplyr::select(NAPQI = Cc_napqi, GSH = Cc_gsh, `NAPQI-GSH` = Cc_napqigsh) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), \(x) format(x, digits = 3))),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Phase I products at 40 minutes (mmol/L). At this therapeutic-range concentration under 1% of APAP goes through CYP2E1."
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Scope.** Only the two ODE modules are packaged. The tissue module and the
  coupled multiscale model are an agent-based Cellular Potts simulation and
  cannot be expressed in rxode2; the paper's multiscale results (Figs 7 to
  17, S1 File Tables 11 to 14) are therefore not reproduced. The APAP-glucuronide
  and APAP-sulfate copies of the PBPK model are also left out: in the paper
  their only input is the conjugate leaving the simulated sinusoid, so they
  have no standalone use. Their parameter values are in Table 2 (`_G` and
  `_S` rows) and S1 File Table 10, and the same structure with those values
  and `kmet = 0` would reproduce them given a liver input.
* **Hepatic metabolism constant.** The standalone PBPK module removes liver
  APAP at `kmet * liver / (kp_liver * fup)` (Table 1, `CLiver -> CMetabolized`).
  The paper prints the rate law but no value for `CLmetab`; the value 9.5 per
  hour is the one in the deposited SBML file. In the multiscale model the
  authors set it to zero and replace the liver with the sinusoid model.
* **Glomerular filtration rate.** Table 2 and S1 File Table 10 give REFSIM
  `pbpk_Qgfr` = 0.714 L/h (the 11.9 mL/min APAP renal clearance of Prescott,
  per a comment in the driver script), and the multiscale driver applies that
  value. The deposited SBML instead computes `Qgfr` from body weight as
  0.039 * BW^0.75 = 0.944 L/h (S1 File Table 2). The packaged model uses the
  REFSIM value as a fixed flow. The choice moves the simulated plasma Cmax by
  under 0.5% and urinary recovery from 3.3% to 4.4% of the dose.
* **Total perfusable volume.** The deposited SBML scales it linearly
  (0.6 L/kg times body weight); S1 File Table 2 and the multiscale driver use
  1.7355 * BW^0.75. Both give 42.0 L at 70 kg, so the reference simulation is
  unaffected; they differ only if `bw` is changed. The packaged model follows
  the SBML.
* **Observed quantity.** Fig 4 plots venous whole-blood concentration against
  plasma data; the multiscale driver converts venous blood to plasma by
  dividing by the blood-to-plasma ratio. The model returns both: `Cvenous`
  (Fig 4) and `Cc` (plasma). With `bp = 1.09` the plasma value is about 8%
  lower.
* **Units.** The SBML PBPK model works in moles; the packaged model works in
  mg so that `Cc` is in mg/L (ug/mL), the unit of Fig 4. The PBPK model is
  linear, so the change of unit does not alter any profile. Table 6 prints
  `sc_kNAPQIGSH` and `sc_kGsh` in mmol/L/s; their rate laws (Table 5) make
  them a second-order constant (L/mmol/s) and a first-order constant (1/s),
  which is how the SBML declares them.
* **Initial glutathione.** Table 6 gives `GSH0` = 9.9 mmol/L, used here; the
  SBML file initialises GSH at 10 mmol/L and the multiscale driver at
  9.9999 mmol/L. GSH barely moves at the Fig 6 APAP concentration, so the
  choice does not affect the figure.
* **CYP2E1 zonation.** In the multiscale model each hepatocyte's
  `sc_Vmax_2E1_APAP` is scaled from 80% (periportal) to 100% (pericentral) of
  the Table 6 value. The standalone module uses the full value.
* **Variability.** The paper's population simulation draws each of 38
  parameters from a normal distribution with 25% CV truncated to 0.75 to 1.25
  times its REFSIM value, inside the multiscale model. No between-subject
  variability is encoded here.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found for this article
  (EuropePMC search, 2026-11-24).
